ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Minimal change disease: 4

A child with a typical minimal-change nephrotic presentation receives standard specialist-directed treatment and rapidly enters remission. Which usual treatment-response feature distinguishes many such cases from more resistant forms of podocyte disease?

  1. Frequent corticosteroid responsiveness in typical childhood disease
  2. Podocyte foot-process effacement
  3. Near-normal glomeruli on light microscopy
  4. No substantial immune deposits on immunofluorescence
  5. Predominantly albumin-rich proteinuria
Answer and explanation

Frequent corticosteroid responsiveness in typical childhood disease

Typical childhood minimal change disease often responds to corticosteroids; atypical or resistant cases require reassessment.

Option explanations

Frequent corticosteroid responsiveness in typical childhood disease: Typical childhood minimal change disease often responds to corticosteroids; atypical or resistant cases require reassessment.

Podocyte foot-process effacement: Electron microscopy detects loss of normal podocyte foot-process architecture in many proteinuric diseases. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Near-normal glomeruli on light microscopy: Minimal change disease can have striking proteinuria despite little visible light-microscopic change. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

No substantial immune deposits on immunofluorescence: Classic minimal change disease lacks the immune-complex staining pattern of membranous nephropathy. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Predominantly albumin-rich proteinuria: Minimal change disease often has relatively selective albumin loss, reflecting altered filtration-barrier function. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
